messages.subject: multiple dynamic plots in shiny
parts:
I tried to make dynamic multiple plots according to the option that the user choose.
If the user choose "ALL", I want to show all plots for each field together in one page.
But it shows multiple plots but all of them are the same, which is the plot of the last field, and if I add local trying to solve this problem, there is no any plots showed.

Is there anyone can help me and point out what the problems probably be?
Thanks very very much.

I used the following code:

output$design <- renderUI({
  if (is.null(dataInput()))
    return()
  if (is.null(input$fieldSelect))
    return()
  if (is.null(input$trialType))
    return()

    if (input$fieldSelect == "ALL")
      fields <- fieldInstances()
    else {
      fields <- input$fieldSelect 
      }

      fieldPlots <- list()
    for(iField in fields){
#       local ({
        fieldName <- iField
        fieldPlots[[fieldName]] <- renderPlot({
          subdata <- droplevels(observedData()[observedData()$FIELDINST == fieldName, ])
          fieldplot2.data.frame(subdata, column = "CHECKFactor",
                                  borderColumns = c("TRIAL", "BLOCK"),
                                  main= fieldName)})
#       })
      }
     do.call(tagList, fieldPlots)
    }                       
})

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: multiple dynamic plots in shiny
parts: Your renderUI should be returning something more like `lapply(fields, plotOutput)`, while each renderPlot should be assigned to a corresponding `output[[fieldName]]`. If possible, you should do the latter outside of the renderUI (unless you can't predict all possible fields in advance). It's OK to have these output[[fieldName]] defined even if the corresponding plotOutput is not visible at the moment on the page; they will generally be smart enough not to execute when they're not currently on the page.
